doc.title: Annie Ross — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Georgia Brown and other singers she admired
summary: Ross recalls sharing a flat with Georgia Brown and praises Nellie Lutcher, Dorothy Donegan, Shirley Horn, Wynton Marsalis and Johnny Mandel.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: You mentioned Georgia Brown earlier. She was another – go ahead.

Georgia Brown and I shared a flat in London. Georgia was powerful. She was totally powerful. She was also weird. I remember she said to me once, “Why” – I played her something that I felt proud about, and she said, “Why is it that everything you do sounds dated?” Boy, that was like, whack. She was a good girl, but she went out to Hollywood, and it messed her up. Values, I’m talking about. What about Nellie Lutcher?
She was wonderful. And Dorothy Donegan.
Dorothy was powerful too. Shirley Horn?
Oh, my God. I heard her do – it was the Johnny Mandel album.
She was wonderful. I loved her. I just wished that so many of my friends didn’t have such a hard time. If I had a lot of money, I’d give it all away to musicians, if you

can find them nowadays, and I’m sure you can. I thought Wynton was incredible on The Shadow of Your Smile. How beautiful. That really was something. And what about Johnny Mandel? Unbelievable. I knew him when he was with the Basie band. We used to call him Johnny MAN-dul. Lovely man. What a heart. What ears. Boy.
